steps.text: Cream butter and sugar together in a large bowl until light and fluffy. Add eggs one at a time, beating well with each addition. Combine flour, baking soda, cinnamon, and cloves; gradually stir into creamed mixture. Combine water and dates; stir into dough along with chopped pecans. Cover and chill for 1 hour.
Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C). Grease cookie sheets. Drop by rounded spoonfuls onto the prepared cookie sheets.
Bake for 8 to 10 minutes in the preheated oven. Allow cookies to cool on baking sheet for 5 minutes before removing to a wire rack to cool completely.

raw_recipe.headline: Date Cookies
raw_recipe.description: These delicious date cookies are subtly spiced with cinnamon and cloves. The dates add a lovely sweetness and chopped pecans add crunch!

review.reviewBody:
These are exactly what they say, nice and chewy. my Dates were a bit dry so i chopped them and heated through on the stove with a few tsp water just to soften them a bit.
definately would make them again

I used half white and half brown sugar. I increased the spices a bit. I found that these were a bit dry but very tasty. They kept very well not like some cake recipes that tend to stick together as they are too moist.

I halved the recipe, but didn't reduce the amount of spices or dates and nuts (I used walnuts instead of pecans). These cookies came out great!! I loved that they didn't have a lot of sugar added to them, since the dates are plenty sweet on their own. This really allowed the date flavor to come through. I do recommend adding some salt and vanilla extract to bring out the flavors ever more, however. And the cookies didn't really spread much while baking--so I pressed them down a little bit right after they came out of the oven. That helped them get the slightly chewier texture that I like. Overall, these are a winner! Thank you for sharing your recipe!

Overall a great recipe for a cakey, chewy cookie. The only tweak I made was to sub 1 cup of oats for one of the cups of flour. Next time I would add some salt and vanilla and toast the pecans for more flavor. I did flatten them before baking as others had suggested and they didn’t spread but held a nice, round cookie shape .

It a really good cookie! I used cold coffee instead of water and a dash of vanilla. It was easy and I didn't cool for 1 hour just kind of let it rest and went ahead and made cookies. My husband is diabetic so used 1 cup of Splenda and 1/3 cup sugar. They came out chewy and wonderful. Thanks!
I followed the recipe except I didn't have pecans so I toasted some walnuts and I didn't have cloves so I used allspice, cinnamon, cardamom, and nutmeg. They were delicious.

I have been looking for a date nut cookie recipe like my moms for years and this has come pretty close to it. It's just missing my mom's special touch. She would make these date nut cookies every year at Christmas and then roll them in powder sugar while they were still warm. I miss those days but now I can now create my own memories with this recipe with my kids. One reviewer suggested this was more of an adult cookie, try the powder sugar and I think you will change your mind.
Pretty tasty- we only added 1/2 the sugar and omitted the nuts, used bobs red mill 1 to 1 baking flour (food allergies) and still good!

I followed the recipe's original "36 portion" measurements -- and I got 61 cookies out of it. I increased baking time to 12 minutes because I have silver reflective cookie sheets. The came out with an excellent texture all over, and through the cookie. The moisture level is perfect, and the use of the clove and cinnamon gave a discrete flavour of a molasses or a spice cookie -- but with a lighter batter instead of dark. The bits of dates, if chopped to proper size, offers a wonderful burst of extra moist chewiness through the cookie. I was extremely pleased with this recipe, and may try out the same excellent batter with other types of fruits such as chopped cherries or perhaps sultanas or figs.
My kind of cookie! I increased the dates by 1/2 because I wanted to use up the fresh dates I had. Added a bit of salt. Baked for 11 minutes and perfect. Will make again for sure.
Added 1 tsp of vanilla extract and swapped out 1 cup of flour for rolled oats. Made half the dough without nuts and half with chopped walnuts. Came out great! 👍

I followed the instructions for half a batch and cut the sugar down to one cup and also added a little splash of vanilla into the water to hydrate the dates. I didn’t have ground clove and added a bit more cinnamon and a little cardamom. They turned out beautiful. I am excited to make them again and I plan to experiment with different flavor combinations like dried cherry and pistachio, apricot and almond, and other dried fruit and nut combinations since the cookies came out so nice. I will definitely be keeping this recipe and experiment with different flavors. We don’t like overly sweet dessert so one cup of sugar, along with this sweetness of the dates was plenty sweet for us. Thanks for a wonderful recipe, definitely a keeper!
Very good. I took the advice of others and doubled the cinnamon, added vanilla extract and the salt. Will make again. Also used walnuts instead of pecans.
Was easy and it had all ingredients I love. Made it as a gift to a kind person

I added candied ginger and a few tsp of molasses. I can’t say why but happy I did. On their own without dates or even raisins just walnuts/pecans alone or none at all because the flavor was outstanding, they would make a delicious yet unfancy cookie. Next time I might add coconut…
I would add a bit more cinnamon and cloves for more flavor. I baked 13 minutes
I will add vanilla next time.
